name: veabird
description: Plan ski and beach trips with live snow, sargassum and crowd forecasts, lodging and flights.

interface.longDescription:
Veabird turns live snow and beach forecasts into trips you can book.

Skiing: tell it your ability (or your group's, kids included), home airport, Epic or Ikon pass and dates. Veabird ranks about 300 resorts worldwide on terrain that fits everyone, snow and crowds for your dates, drive or flight time, and pass coverage, and explains every pick. Ask about any resort for today's ski score, the 7-day snow forecast, terrain mix and crowd outlook.

Beaches: 1,400+ resorts in the Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico, Mexico's Pacific coast and Hawaii, scored 0-100 for any date up to a year out, with sargassum seaweed, weather, water temperature, waves, crowds, hurricanes and travel advisories. Veabird can suggest a better beach nearby when the seaweed is bad.

Trips: for any ski or beach resort, Veabird gives conditions for your dates, places to stay with nightly prices and photos filtered by your budget, vacation-rental searches, flight searches from your home airport to the best gateway airports, and extras like lift tickets, ski rentals and tours.

What it accesses: Veabird's public forecast data and hotel rates from our partner LiteAPI. It reads only what you ask about (places, dates, party size, ability, pass, budget). It never books, pays or changes anything: every tool is a read-only lookup, and booking happens on partner sites you choose to open. No account or setup needed.

Limitations: forecasts are modeled estimates, not safety guidance; dates beyond 16 days use climate outlooks. Veabird doesn't quote airfares yet; it opens live fare searches. Lodging, flight and rental links are partner links; Veabird may earn a commission at no extra cost, and partners never affect forecasts or rankings.
defaultPrompt: Where should we ski in late January? Two intermediates and a 7-year-old, Ikon pass, flying from Dallas.
Plan 4 nights at Breckenridge in February for 2 adults, under $350 a night, flying from Chicago.
Is there seaweed in Tulum next week? If so, which nearby beach is better?
